public_rationale: The CNBC example supports the narrower observation that media amplified an alarming employment forecast. It does not predict the destruction of all employment: it reports a conditional forecast about college graduates and attributes it to McDermott. This is material counterevidence to Zitron's literal characterization, but one article cannot settle a claim about the media generally. The broader claim that future universal job destruction is a myth also remains untestable without a specified scenario.
limitations: The accessible evidence is not a representative media sample.
The New York Times article was inaccessible.
No conclusion is drawn about whether McDermott's forecast will come true.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The idea of agentic AI that will destroy all employment is a myth perpetuated by the media.

statement.excerpt: Yet the media continues to perpetuate the myth of some sort of present or future “agentic AI” that will destroy all employment.

our_interpretation: The checkable observation concerns how contemporary media presents employment displacement by agentic AI.
The plain reading of all employment is universal elimination of employment. The alternative reading of widespread displacement is materially weaker and is flagged.
Perpetuate can include amplifying an attributed prediction; attribution alone does not disprove that part of the criticism.
For the ongoing observation, use January through March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication. No reporting period was supplied.
The assertion that every future employment-elimination scenario is a myth cannot be settled by current employment data or by inspecting a few articles.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary coverage repeatedly promotes agentic AI eliminating all employment as a credible or established prospect, with evidence sufficient to assess the alleged gap between that presentation and its factual basis.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently representative examination shows that the alleged coverage instead concerns limited displacement, attributed uncertainty, or explicitly qualified scenarios. Narrower wording in the named examples contradicts their use as examples of universal elimination but does not establish what all media says.
